questions.q: During Covid-19 the world was busy in preparing 1.5 billion learners for the new normal, i.e., ____ learning.
questions.explanation: School closures during the pandemic pushed about 1.5 billion learners worldwide into remote (online, distance) learning, which became the new normal. Physical classroom learning was exactly what was disrupted.

questions.q: To develop learner readiness for online learning, training sessions on ____ are helpful.
questions.explanation: Online learners need to know online etiquette, manage their own time, and study independently, so training on all three builds readiness for online learning.

questions.q: The typical picture of a teacher being a dispenser of knowledge to the students has been replaced by that of a ____.
questions.explanation: In learner-centred and online education, the teacher guides, supports and scaffolds students' own construction of knowledge, acting as a facilitator rather than a one-way transmitter of information.

questions.q: In 2018, Global Education and Skills Forum noted that the 'future' teacher would need the 5 skills to thrive in the 21st century. Which of the following is not one of them?
questions.explanation: The forum's list of future-teacher skills included strong social skills, data analysis and an external focus, among others. Strictness was not on it; the emphasis is on flexible, facilitative teaching rather than rigid control.

questions.q: Participatory education demands ____ so as to build a needs-based approach to teaching.
questions.explanation: Participatory education adapts teaching to learners' needs and involves them actively, which calls for creativity in designing activities and methods. Stubbornness works against such a flexible, needs-based approach.

questions.q: Students who consider intelligence as a malleable entity tend to focus on their obstacles instead of goals.
questions.explanation: Students with an incremental (growth) view of intelligence believe ability can be developed through effort, so they focus on learning goals and persist through difficulties. Dwelling on obstacles is more typical of students who see intelligence as fixed.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a principle to enhance student learning.
options: What students already know affects their learning
Students' cognitive development and learning is limited by the general stages of development.
The acquisition of knowledge and skills in the long term depends largely on practice.
questions.explanation: The actual principle (APA's top 20 principles) states that students' cognitive development and learning are NOT limited by general stages of development, so this option reverses it. The other options are genuine principles: prior knowledge, context and practice all shape learning.

questions.q: ____ feedback to students is important for learning.
questions.explanation: Effective feedback is clear, explanatory, specific and timely: it tells students why something is right or wrong and how to improve. Unclear, late or harsh feedback reduces its value for learning.

questions.q: Mastery goals are those that are geared towards the acquisition or improvement of____.
options: Number of students in a classroom
questions.explanation: Mastery (learning) goals focus on developing competence, that is, acquiring or improving skills and understanding. Performance goals, by contrast, focus on demonstrating ability relative to others.

questions.q: The vast majority of formative assessment is____.
questions.explanation: Formative assessment happens continuously during instruction, mostly through informal means such as questioning, observation and quick checks for understanding. Formal, written tests are more typical of summative assessment.
